backlog.spec: Append MACCS keys (rdkit.Chem.MACCSkeys.GenMACCSKeys converted to a numpy array) to the features, and cut Morgan fpSize from 2048 to 512. This gives a more compact, generalizable substructure representation alongside the descriptors.
backlog.title: Add MACCS keys and reduce Morgan bits

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, map y to normal scores with scipy.stats.rankdata and norm.ppf((rank-0.5)/n), then rescale to the original mean and sd. Fit the ridge and XGB on the transformed target. Map the predictions back by interpolating np.interp against the sorted transformed values and sorted original y. Keep the rest of the pipeline unchanged.
backlog.title: Rank-Gaussian target transform

backlog.spec: Change the two-stage recipe so stage1 uses n_estimators=300 (squared error) and stage2 uses n_estimators=300 (absolute error) with continuation from stage1. Keep all other params the same. This tests whether more L2 warm-up and fewer L1 rounds helps.
backlog.title: Stage round counts 300/300

backlog.spec: Extend featurize_one so the feature vector also contains the 167 MACCS keys (rdMACCSkeys.GenMACCSKeys converted to numpy) and a feature-invariant Morgan count fingerprint (rdFingerprintGenerator.GetMorganGenerator with atomInvariantsGenerator=rdFingerprintGenerator.GetMorganFeatureAtomInvGen(), radius 2, 1024 bits). Concatenate these after the existing Morgan count bits and descriptors. Everything else in fit_predict stays identical.
backlog.title: Add MACCS keys and FCFP-style feature-invariant fingerprints

backlog.spec: Add count-based atom-pair fingerprints (rdFingerprintGenerator.GetAtomPairGenerator, fpSize 1024) to the feature vector. These capture topological distances between pharmacophore-like atoms, which is complementary to the Morgan environments.
backlog.title: Add Morgan with chirality-free feature invariants and atom pair counts

backlog.spec: Before the two-stage XGBoost fit, fit a quick stage-1 squared-error XGBoost on the full feature matrix with 150 rounds. Keep only the columns whose total gain importance is in the top 400 (use get_booster().get_score(importance_type='total_gain') and map names back to column indices). Train both stage 1 and stage 2 on the reduced matrix. Feature selection uses training labels only, and it is done inside fit_predict on each fold.
backlog.title: Importance-based feature pruning before the residual boosters

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, compute Morgan count fingerprints (radius 2, 2048 bits) for train and test, then fit sklearn SVR with a precomputed Tanimoto (min-max / Jaccard for counts) kernel K(a,b)=sum(min(a,b))/sum(max(a,b)) on the training residuals y - base_tr, with C=1.0 and epsilon=0.05. Predict the test residuals from the test-vs-train kernel. Final output is base_te + 0.5*xgb_pred + 0.5*svr_pred, i.e. average the existing XGBoost residual prediction with the SVR residual prediction. Use seed nowhere in SVR since it is deterministic.
backlog.title: Tanimoto-kernel SVR ensemble member

backlog.spec: After computing the final prediction (ridge base + two-stage XGBoost residual), add a small nearest-neighbour correction. Compute 2048-bit Morgan bit vectors for train and test, get the Tanimoto similarity of each test molecule to all training molecules, and take its k=5 most similar training molecules. Obtain out-of-fold training residuals by running an inner 5-fold KFold (shuffled with the given seed) over the same full pipeline is too slow, so instead use the in-bag residuals from a single extra XGBoost fit with subsample=0.7 and use only out-of-bag-like shrinkage: multiply the correction by 0.3. Concretely, correction_i = 0.3 * sum_j w_ij * r_j / sum_j w_ij over the k neighbours, where w_ij is the Tanimoto similarity and r_j is the training residual y_j - (base_j + stage2 prediction on train). Add the correction to the test prediction. Keep the shrinkage factor 0.3 fixed so the change cannot do much damage.
backlog.title: Tanimoto k-nearest-neighbour residual correction

backlog.spec: Choose the stage-2 round count per fold instead of hard-coding 400. Inside fit_predict, split the training set with GroupKFold(n_splits=4) using Murcko scaffold strings (Chem.Scaffolds.MurckoScaffold.MurckoScaffoldSmiles, falling back to the SMILES itself when it returns an empty string) as groups. For each inner split, run the full recipe (ridge base, stage-1 200 squared-error rounds, then stage-2 L1) and record the inner-validation MAE after 100, 200, 400, 600 and 800 stage-2 rounds using a single fit with staged evaluation (fit 800 rounds once, then predict with iteration_range). Average the MAE curve over the 4 inner folds, pick the round count with the lowest mean, and refit on the full training set with that value. Keep every other hyper-parameter fixed.
backlog.title: Inner scaffold-grouped CV for the number of L1 rounds

backlog.spec: Add features to phys_one for the ridge base: formal charge sum, counts of carboxylic acid, basic amine and amide SMARTS matches, fraction of sp3 carbons (rdMolDescriptors.CalcFractionCSP3), and number of rings. Use Chem.MolFromSmarts patterns compiled once at module level. Keep Ridge alpha=1.0 on the standardized features, so the residual booster sees a better base.
backlog.title: Ionization and polarity ridge features

backlog.spec: Extend phys_one, which currently returns TPSA, MolLogP, NumHDonors, NumHAcceptors, MolWt, NumRotatableBonds and the aromatic-atom fraction, with five cheap ionization/polarity terms computed from the same molecule: (1) count of carboxylic-acid matches via SMARTS '[CX3](=O)[OX2H1]', (2) count of basic amine matches via SMARTS '[NX3;H2,H1;!$(N[#6]=[O,N,S])]', (3) formal charge sum from Chem.GetFormalCharge, (4) Descriptors.NumAromaticRings, (5) Descriptors.FractionCSP3. Cache compiled SMARTS patterns at module level. Everything downstream is unchanged: StandardScaler, Ridge(alpha=1.0), then the two-stage XGBoost on the residuals. Permeability is dominated by ionization state at physiological pH, which neither logP nor TPSA alone encodes, so the linear base is the right place for these.
backlog.title: Ionization and polarity features in the ridge base

backlog.spec: Extend phys_one with extra descriptors (NumAromaticRings, FractionCSP3, HeavyAtomCount, RingCount, MolMR, LabuteASA, charge-related counts such as the number of carboxylic acids and basic amines via SMARTS) and use RidgeCV with alphas 0.1 to 100 for the base model. A better base lets the trees fit a smaller residual.
backlog.title: Stronger linear base with more physchem

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, split the training molecules into 4 folds grouped by Murcko scaffold (MurckoScaffold.MurckoScaffoldSmiles, group by the scaffold string, assign whole groups to folds with a seeded shuffle). Use the first inner fold as a validation set for stage2 only: train stage1 and stage2 with an eval_set on the validation residuals, early_stopping_rounds=50, and n_estimators up to 1000 for stage2, then refit on all training data with the best iteration count (best_iteration+1 rounds). Keep the objectives and other parameters unchanged.
backlog.title: Inner scaffold-grouped early stopping for the boosting rounds

backlog.spec: In featurize_one, drop the Morgan count fingerprint and keep only the RDKit descriptor vector (Descriptors.descList). Caco-2 permeability is driven by physchem properties (TPSA, logP, HBD, etc.), and fingerprint bits may not generalize across unseen scaffolds. Keep the rest of the pipeline unchanged.
backlog.title: Descriptor-only features

backlog.spec: After the current two-stage fit, compute in-sample absolute residuals on the training set. Drop the 5% of training molecules with the largest errors and refit stage1 and stage2 on the remaining molecules with the same params. Predict with the refit model. The ridge base stays fit on all the data.
backlog.title: Trimmed refit after residual screening

backlog.spec: After computing the final prediction, compute Tanimoto similarity on binary Morgan bits between each test molecule and the training molecules. Use the training residuals (y minus in-sample base plus stage predictions is overfit, so use y - base_tr instead of the boosted residuals). For each test molecule take the similarity-weighted mean of that residual over the top 5 neighbors with similarity above 0.5, shrink it by 0.3, and add it to the prediction. Leave molecules with no such neighbors unchanged.
backlog.title: kNN residual correction

backlog.spec: The incumbent fits 200 squared-error rounds then 400 absolute-error rounds, both at learning_rate 0.03. Change only the schedule: use learning_rate 0.02 with 300 squared-error rounds for stage 1 and 700 absolute-error rounds for stage 2 (same warm start via xgb_model=stage1.get_booster(), same depth/subsample/colsample/min_child_weight). The intent is to test whether the accepted two-stage gain is sensitive to how much of the total shrinkage is spent on L2 versus L1; a longer, slower L1 tail should fit the median more carefully without over-fitting because the L2 stage has already captured the smooth trend. Nothing else in the file changes.
backlog.title: Rebalance the two boosting stages

backlog.spec: In the two-stage XGBoost recipe, change only the stage-1 squared-error model. Use learning_rate=0.06 with n_estimators=100 instead of learning_rate=0.03 with 200 rounds. Keep stage 2 at 400 L1 rounds with learning_rate=0.03, so the stage-1 contribution is roughly half of its current total shrinkage. The goal is to test whether a shorter squared-error warm start helps the L1 stage.
backlog.title: Stage-1 learning-rate and round pairing

backlog.spec: Set max_depth=4, min_child_weight=5, reg_lambda=5, colsample_bytree=0.2, and subsample=0.7 in params. With only about 580 training molecules per fold and unseen scaffolds, shallower and more regularized trees may generalize better.
backlog.title: Stronger XGB regularization

backlog.spec: Make the boosted residual correction depend on how well the test molecule is covered by the training set. Compute Morgan bit vectors and, for each test molecule, its maximum Tanimoto similarity s to any training molecule. Define a gate g = clip((s - 0.2) / 0.3, 0.0, 1.0), so molecules with max similarity at or below 0.2 get g=0 and those at or above 0.5 get g=1. Return base_te + g * stage2.predict(Xte) instead of base_te + stage2.predict(Xte). For far-out-of-domain scaffolds the fingerprint-driven correction is mostly noise and the smooth physchem ridge is the safer predictor, which matters here because every fold tests on unseen skeletons. Keep the two thresholds fixed at 0.2 and 0.5; no tuning inside the fold.
backlog.title: Similarity-gated shrinkage toward the ridge base

backlog.spec: Add six whole-molecule topology descriptors to phys_one, which currently returns seven values: number of rings (rdMolDescriptors.CalcNumRings), number of aromatic rings, number of saturated rings, number of bridgehead atoms (CalcNumBridgeheadAtoms), number of spiro atoms (CalcNumSpiroAtoms), and the fraction of heavy atoms that belong to the Murcko scaffold (heavy atoms of MurckoScaffold.GetScaffoldForMol divided by total heavy atoms, 0.0 when the scaffold is empty). Standardize and fit Ridge(alpha=1.0) on the 13 features as before, then run the unchanged two-stage XGBoost on the residuals. Rigid, highly fused ring systems permeate differently from flexible chains, and the current base has only NumRotatableBonds and aromatic fraction to express that.
backlog.title: Ring-system and scaffold-topology features in the ridge base

backlog.spec: Set learning_rate to 0.02 for both stages. Change stage1 n_estimators to 300 and stage2 n_estimators to 800. Everything else stays the same.
backlog.title: Longer MAE stage with lower learning rate

backlog.spec: Keep the entire pipeline unchanged, but wrap it so the final predictions are clipped to the range [min(train_y) - 0.2*range, max(train_y) + 0.2*range], where range = max(train_y) - min(train_y). Also apply an explicit mean-centering: subtract np.median(train_y) from y before fitting the Ridge baseline and add it back to the final output, so the boosted models see a zero-median target. This guards against extrapolation on unusual test molecules.
backlog.title: Log-target sanity transform and prediction clipping

backlog.spec: Replace the Ridge physchem base with a shallow XGBoost base. Fit XGBRegressor(max_depth=2, n_estimators=150, learning_rate=0.05, subsample=0.8, objective='reg:absoluteerror', random_state=seed, n_jobs=8) on the seven unscaled physchem features, using the training fold only, to get base_tr and base_te. Keep the two-stage Morgan-plus-descriptor XGBoost residual model on y - base_tr unchanged, so the first stage has the same offset form as now.
backlog.title: Shallow gradient-boosted physchem base instead of Ridge

backlog.spec: In featurize_one, also compute MACCS keys (rdkit.Chem.MACCSkeys.GenMACCSKeys, converted to a numpy array of 167 bits) and an atom-pair count fingerprint (rdFingerprintGenerator.GetAtomPairGenerator(fpSize=1024).GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy). Concatenate them to the existing fp+desc vector. The model is unchanged.
backlog.title: Add RDKit 2D pharmacophore/MACCS and atom-pair count features

backlog.spec: Keep the architecture and the two-stage schedule exactly as they are, and change only the regularization terms in the shared params dict: set min_child_weight=6 (from 3), gamma=0.5 (new, minimum loss reduction per split), reg_lambda=5.0 (from the default 1.0) and max_depth=5 (from 6). With only ~580 training molecules per fold and scaffold-disjoint test folds, the incumbent trees are likely splitting on fingerprint bits that are present in a handful of molecules; harder split acceptance and heavier leaf shrinkage should trade a little training fit for generalization to unseen skeletons. Everything else, including the 200 + 400 round split and learning_rate 0.03, is unchanged.
backlog.title: Stronger leaf and split regularization

backlog.spec: Keep everything in fit_predict as it is (ridge physchem base, Morgan counts + RDKit descriptors, stage1 200 rounds reg:squarederror then stage2 400 rounds reg:absoluteerror warm-started from stage1), but instead of fitting one two-stage model, fit 5 independent copies with random_state = seed, seed+1, ..., seed+4 and also vary subsample/colsample row-column draws only through that seed (no other parameter changes). Average the 5 test predictions with the mean, then add the ridge base prediction. Reduce n_jobs to 8 still (XGBoost handles the threads; the models are fit sequentially). This is pure variance reduction on the exact incumbent recipe, which single-seed bagging experiments hinted at (-0.0035) but never combined with the two-stage fit. Keep runtime in check: 5 x 600 rounds on ~580 training rows is still well under the 10-minute budget.
backlog.title: Seed-averaged two-stage XGBoost

backlog.spec: Keep the feature set, Ridge baseline and two-stage structure. Change the XGBoost hyperparameters to reduce overfitting on only 728 molecules: max_depth=4, min_child_weight=5, reg_lambda=5.0, reg_alpha=0.1, gamma=0.1, subsample=0.7, colsample_bytree=0.2. Keep learning_rate=0.03 and the stage1 squared-error and stage2 absolute-error objectives as they are.
backlog.title: Stronger regularization of the XGBoost residual stages

backlog.spec: Wrap the two XGB stages in a loop over 5 different seeds (seed*10+i) and average the stage2 predictions. This reduces variance from subsampling and column sampling. Reduce n_jobs overhead if needed to stay under the time limit.
backlog.title: Seed-bagged XGB

backlog.spec: After computing the XGBoost residual prediction, compute the Jaccard similarity between each test molecule's Morgan bit vector (radius 2, 2048 bits) and all training molecules' bit vectors. For each test molecule take the k=5 most similar training molecules, weight them by similarity raised to power 2, and compute a weighted average of their out-of-model residuals (y - base_tr - in-sample stage2 prediction on train). Add this kNN residual correction, scaled by 0.3, to the final prediction. Use the same procedure for train residuals only through the stored training values; no leakage across the test set.
backlog.title: Tanimoto nearest-neighbour residual correction

memo: Helped: swapping RF for XGBoost with L1 loss (0.3828, -0.0589 vs the 0.4417 start). Adding a ridge on six RDKit physchem descriptors plus aromatic-atom features, with XGB fitting its residuals, gave 0.3755/0.3715. A two-stage XGB residual fit (200 rounds of squared-error, then L1) is the current incumbent at 0.3658/0.3652 over 2 runs. Noise-level or no gain (noise sd about 0.0037): bagged XGB 0.3793, 6-model ensemble 0.3795, winsorized targets 0.3727, Avalon+ErG 0.3710, LightGBM, CatBoost, GP, MLP, Tanimoto kernel ridge, MACCS, 3D shape, calibration, quantile correction, polynomial or sparse-L1 ridge bases. Tree and Morgan tuning looks saturated. Next: vary the two-stage recipe (round counts, learning rate, Huber loss for stage two), combine small gains with it (bagging, Avalon/ErG, winsorizing), and add polarity/ionization descriptors (TPSA, HBD, charge) to the ridge. Avoid specs that abort at the engine.
